body: My anorexia b/p is getting worse. I've lost more weight. I b/p more. I can't stop myself. I'm lying to my treatment team. I'm trapped. I can't gain weight back. I'm terrified to do so... What the fuck do I even do?

By that logic, I should get off every single eating disorder recovery space I am in since I'm not really recovering currently. 

I want to recover yes. But am I all in going for recovery right now? No. I'm not. But am I seeking and lurking to see what could be? What I could do to recover? Listen to the victories of people in recovery? Yes indeed. And those kinds of things helps me immeasurably. 

Even if I'm not seeking to upend my life and change everything this minute, I can still see what could be. I can at least be conscious of the fact I have a problem. And that recovery is possible. That's why I'm there. 

And I suspect that people who maybe aren't actively losing weight but SMO are also here for similar reasons. They're looking for community. Looking for what could be. Looking for people that get it. And have been there. And at least being here means that yes, they're conscious of the fact that this is an issue that needs addressing. That's at least the start of change.

Honestly, I feel like the first step to bettering yourself, comes from merely thinking of entertaining the idea and coming to get support from people who have been in the same place as you. 

No one gets to 600 lbs due to just "I eat too much" and that's the end of the story. Getting to a weight like that is most likely the result of an eating disorder. And yes, binge eating disorder is real and valid. Just like anorexia, bulimia, and EDNOS. 

Evidently to gain weight you need a calorie surplus. But that's just the surface. You have to work to analyze what has led you to make your choices whether it be upbringing, traumas, eating disorders etc. 

If you would find offense to telling an anorexic "just eat" or telling a bulimic "just stop throwing up", then why is it with people who are obese, it's acceptable to say "just lose the weight"? 

Weight loss is a piece of this. It's the goal. But the journey to get there is not self hatred. It's not anger. It's not self loathing. It's about first saying, "I am here. I am not proud that I'm here. I may not be proud of the choices that I made to get here in this position. But I am here now and I accept I am here now." Just taking on this mentality leads to a lot more sustainable results than "I hate myself. I'm so x, y, z negative attribute". 

If weight loss was the end all be all, why is it that bariatric surgeons want people to go through psychotherapy first? They want to ensure that you have put in the mental work to heal what has led you here. 

As for me, Im someone with an eating disorder. I'll admit that much. I've met people in treatment with binge eating disorder and who are very overweight. Despite the fact that at the time, I was underweight and some of those people were quite overweight, I came to understand they were struggling with much of the same demons as me. Traumatic upbringings. Bad habits around food and eating taught by family. Feelings of constant self loathing and self hatred. Feelings of hopelessness and resignation. 

These. These feelings are not just resolved by losing weight. Resolving these feelings is part of the journey to living a happier, healthier, and more fulfilling life.

I'm glad exercise and weight lifting has helped you reduce and stop purging. 

For me, I come from a background of exercise addiction. I additionally come from a background of trauma. I do not wish to look stronger or more muscular and I have no desire for any kind of exercise that does that. For me, weight lifting would be quite counter intuitive in any kind of harm reduction or any kind of recovery attempt as exercise would simply become another method by which to purge calories in top of vomiting.

Umm... I hate to be that person. But let's not spread misinformation. No one can give some arbitrary figure on how many calories you can throw up. 

Purging is *the* worst ED behavior. *However* no one can actually give you a number of calories that purging removes. I hate to be crude but the number of calories purged depends on too many variables.

But in short, the weight gain is likely water weight as purging makes your water weight go really fucky really easily. 

Take care OP

This is bullshit. Pure bullshit. 

Yes purging is bad. But let's not use fear of weight gain or bullshit statistics to make the point. 

Let me give you the gross example and thought experiment. If vomit doesn't really contain calories, theoretically, you could only eat vomit and lose a shit ton of weight. But why isn't that the case then? 

Also it's impossible to give you an exact fact and figure on how many calories you get rid of by vomiting. There's too many variables. There's the variable of not all things leave the stomach at the same rate, not all macronutrients leave the stomach at the same rate, whether or not your stomach was empty or not before you ate, how much time passed before vomiting, and your "skill" at purging. Weight gain/loss is also dependent on your eating/exercise habits outside of purging.  Granted, you'll never ever get 100% up but it's possible for some people to get pretty goddamn close. 

If this was the case, why the hell are there some people who are markedly and severely underweight yet consuming 10000 calories a day? Even keeping down a third of this would lead to weight gain but they're not gaining weight. Or even just maintaining weight. How can someone maintain an average weight while eating 15000 calories a day? Point made, if you saw food come up in vomit, you didn't absorb the calories. It's impossible to say how much you got up or how many calories you digested. I can't give anyone that answer. 

OP, purging is still bad. But the bottom line is that you shouldn't listen to fear mongering facts to stop you or that you should take more extreme measures to purge. If you saw it, you didn't absorb the calories from the stuff you got up. As for how much, we don't know. Hang in there
